title: Hole cycles: reaming, boring, fine boring and dwell at depth (G85/G86/G89/G76/G82), per post

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat), after a feature comparison with the open-source project stevecad/camlib: "We wanna cover some of the toolpaths and things like that at first." and, on the suggested picks: "Lets create issues on your suggestions, they made sense." On sources: "We should use perplexity to find literature on those types of toolpaths and not copy them straight up".

What is missing: hole making has drilling and tapping cycles only. There is no reaming, boring, fine boring or dwell-at-depth cycle, and no spot-face / counterbore dwell. The tool kinds (reamer, spot drill, countersink, centre drill) are open issue 897; this issue is the cycles and their posted output.

Wanted, as cycle choices on the drilling operation (a user parameter with a default, never hard-wired):
- Reaming: feed in, feed out (G85 where the post has it, expanded moves otherwise).
- Boring: feed in, spindle stop, rapid out (G86); feed in, dwell, feed out (G89).
- Fine boring: feed in, oriented spindle stop, shift off the wall, rapid out (G76 on a mill), with the shift amount and direction as parameters. A post or machine with no spindle orientation refuses it by name rather than posting a retract that drags the tip up the wall.
- Dwell at depth for spot facing and counterboring (G82), in the unit each post expects.

Safety: every post either writes the cycle correctly for its dialect, expands it to plain moves, or refuses by name. A dwell is never silently dropped or written in the wrong unit (seconds against milliseconds). The canned cycle and its expanded form remove the same stock in simulation.

Sources: RS-274 / ISO 6983 and each control maker's published programming manual for the cycle words, found by a literature search (Perplexity) at the start of the work and cited in the PR. camlib is a feature list only: no code is copied or adapted from it.

Done means: each cycle generates, simulates and posts on Fanuc, Haas, Heidenhain, Sinumerik, grblHAL and PathPilot as a canned cycle, an expansion or a named refusal, pinned by a golden per post; an MCP parameter for the cycle choice; a fine bore on a machine without spindle orientation is refused in a test. Not exercised on real controls unless the PR says otherwise.
